title: fix(cuda-graph): fix warmup regression with shape guards during capture/replay
author: Alex Chen
description: Summary: This PR fixes a warmup/regression observed when using CUDA graph capture/replay in combination with shape guards. After recent kernel scheduling and continuous-batching changes, we started seeing failed graph replays or incorrect warmup behavior when shape guards used narrow input shapes that later expanded. Root cause: when a captured graph is replayed under a different shape guard we were incorrectly assuming the KV cache and per-layer buffer offsets were compatible, which led to occasional OOMs and throughput regressions during warmup. Changes: 1) Add stricter shape-guard compatibility checks at replay time and fall back to re-capture when incompatible. 2) Improve warmup path to pre-allocate KV cache ranges based on the superset shape in the guard, avoiding repeated realloc until after the first successful replay. 3) Add a lightweight capture fingerprint to detect kernel-subgraph layout changes (e.g., due to scheduling tweaks) and force safe re-capture when fingerprints differ. 4) Add targeted unit and integration tests that simulate dynamic batching and guard-promotions. Motivation: avoid a class of regressions where a previously captured graph would be reused in an unsafe shape context, degrading throughput and risking OOMs. This PR is a hotfix targeted at recent regressions flagged by ENG-1632; it also hardens the replay logic for future scheduling changes. Testing & Benchmarks: local GPU integration tests, CI GPU matrix, and a small perf harness (benchmarks/graph_replay_bench.py) show warmup latency down to baseline and throughput restored to pre-regression numbers (end-to-end throughput +1.6% vs broken baseline). Checklist: - [x] Reproduce regression locally and in CI - [x] Add unit tests for shape-guard compatibility - [x] Add integration test for capture/replay with dynamic batch growth - [x] Add benchmark to track warmup latency - [x] Update docs/perf/cuda-graph.md with guidance on guard compatibility Related PRs: pr-26890, pr-27645, pr-26234. Linear: ENG-1632. Notes: This change is conservative: when in doubt the runtime will re-capture instead of silently replaying incompatible graphs. No public API changes.
